Her menses have also become unpredictable.

encounters.cc: 6-month history of increasing fatigue, heat intolerance, palpitations, and proximal muscle weakness

lines: 6-month history of increasing fatigue, heat intolerance, palpitations, and proximal muscle weakness

The patient with Graves disease, thyroid-associated orbitopathy, history of antithyroid drug-induced agranulocytosis, and status post radioiodine ablation returns for follow-up six months after initial diagnosis.

She presents with a 6-month history of increasing fatigue, heat intolerance, palpitations, 10-pound weight loss despite increased appetite, and difficulty climbing stairs and rising from a seated position.
Her medical history is significant for Graves' disease, for which she has been noncompliant with her medications.
- Radioiodine thyroid ablation (performed 8 weeks prior to index encounter)
- Prednisone 40 mg oral daily (tapering regimen for ophthalmopathy prophylaxis)
- Acetaminophen 500 mg oral every 6 hours as needed for fever or pain
Methimazole (severe adverse reaction: agranulocytosis), Contrast dye (anaphylaxis)
On physical examination, she has a fine tremor, an enlarged thyroid gland without nodules, and a resting heart rate of 102 bpm.
Muscle strength is 3/5 in the proximal muscles of the lower extremities and 4/5 in the upper extremities.
Reflexes are brisk, and there is mild muscle atrophy in the thighs.

encounters.cc: 2-day history of sore throat and fever with progressive worsening

lines: 2-day history of sore throat and fever with progressive worsening
The patient with Graves disease, thyroid-associated orbitopathy, and history of antithyroid drug-induced agranulocytosis presents to the emergency department.
She reports that her symptoms have progressively worsened despite symptomatic treatment with acetaminophen.
- Radioiodine thyroid ablation (performed 8 weeks prior to index encounter)
She has been on methimazole for the past 6 months.
- Prednisone 40 mg oral daily (tapering regimen for ophthalmopathy prophylaxis)
- Acetaminophen 500 mg oral every 6 hours as needed for fever or pain
Methimazole (severe adverse reaction: agranulocytosis), Contrast dye (anaphylaxis)
Her temperature is 38.9°C (102°F), blood pressure is 130/85 mmHg, pulse is 88/min, and respiratory rate is 16/min.
Physical examination reveals pharyngeal erythema without exudates, and no cervical lymphadenopathy is palpable.
Her thyroid is diffusely enlarged with a bruit.
No rashes or joint swelling are noted.

encounters.cc: Worsening confusion, agitation, and high fever over the past day

lines: Worsening confusion, agitation, and high fever over the past day

This 38-year-old female with Graves disease, thyroid-associated orbitopathy, and prior antithyroid drug-induced agranulocytosis, status post radioiodine ablation, returns to the emergency department and is brought by her partner due to worsening confusion and agitation over the past day.
Over the past three days, she has experienced fever, chills, and a sore throat but did not seek medical attention.
She has a history of untreated hyperthyroidism diagnosed eight months ago but discontinued follow-up because she felt "her symptoms were manageable.".
- Radioiodine thyroid ablation (performed 8 weeks prior to index encounter)
- Prednisone 40 mg oral daily (tapering regimen for ophthalmopathy prophylaxis)
- Acetaminophen 500 mg oral every 6 hours as needed for fever or pain
Methimazole (severe adverse reaction: agranulocytosis), Contrast dye (anaphylaxis)
Temperature is 39.7°C (103.5°F), pulse is 140/min and irregular, blood pressure is 150/80 mmHg, and respiratory rate is 22/min.
On arrival, she is restless, disoriented, and diaphoretic.
Physical examination reveals warm, moist skin, a fine tremor of both hands, and brisk reflexes.
Laboratory studies reveal: TSH <0.01 μU/mL Free T4 6.4 ng/dL Total T3 350 ng/dL
ECG shows atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response.

lines: Anterior neck discomfort that began a week ago without palpitations or weight changes

She denies palpitations or significant weight changes.
- Radioiodine thyroid ablation (performed 8 weeks prior to index encounter)
- Prednisone 40 mg oral daily (tapering regimen for ophthalmopathy prophylaxis)
- Acetaminophen 500 mg oral every 6 hours as needed for fever or pain
Methimazole (severe adverse reaction: agranulocytosis), Contrast dye (anaphylaxis)
Temperature is 38.1°C (100.6°F), blood pressure is 122/74 mmHg, pulse is 102/min, and respiratory rate is 16/min
Palpation of the anterior neck reveals a mildly enlarged, tender thyroid gland without discrete nodules.
Cardiopulmonary and neurologic exams are unremarkable.
The patient is treated with NSAIDs for symptomatic relief.

encounters.cc: Acute visual changes, severe orbital pain, and eyelid swelling

lines: Acute visual changes, severe orbital pain, and eyelid swelling
The patient with Graves disease, thyroid-associated orbitopathy, and status post radioiodine ablation presents with acute visual changes, severe orbital pain, and eyelid swelling.
She also reports increased anxiety and difficulty sleeping.
Her past medical history is significant for Graves' disease diagnosed 6 months ago, for which she received radioiodine therapy 8 weeks prior.
- Radioiodine thyroid ablation (performed 8 weeks prior to index encounter)
- Prednisone 40 mg oral daily (tapering regimen for ophthalmopathy prophylaxis)
- Acetaminophen 500 mg oral every 6 hours as needed for fever or pain
Methimazole (severe adverse reaction: agranulocytosis), Contrast dye (anaphylaxis)
On physical examination, her heart rate is 102 beats per minute, and she has a fine tremor of her outstretched hands.
Her thyroid gland is non-tender and has decreased in size compared to previous examinations.
She also has mild proptosis and periorbital edema.

encounters.cc: Acute onset palpitations and fatigue lasting 3 hours

lines: Acute onset palpitations and fatigue lasting 3 hours
A 42-year-old woman with Graves disease, orbitopathy, and prior radioiodine ablation presents to the emergency department with palpitations and fatigue that started 3 hours ago.
- Radioiodine thyroid ablation (performed 8 weeks prior to index encounter)
- Prednisone 40 mg oral daily (tapering regimen for ophthalmopathy prophylaxis)
- Acetaminophen 500 mg oral every 6 hours as needed for fever or pain
Methimazole (severe adverse reaction: agranulocytosis), Contrast dye (anaphylaxis)
She denies chest pain, shortness of breath, or syncope.
On examination, her blood pressure is 132/86 mmHg, heart rate is 160 beats per minute and irregular, respiratory rate is 18 breaths per minute, and oxygen saturation is 98% on room air.
Her thyroid gland is not enlarged, and there is no tremor.
An electrocardiogram (ECG) shows an irregularly irregular rhythm, absent P waves, and varying R-R intervals.
